title: Winged Beans
description: Winged Beans (tua poo) or Wing Beans, as used in Thai cooking, information by Kasma Loha-unchit.

author: Kasma Loha-unchit
body:
Thai Ingredient Index

See also: Information on Bitter Melon and Sataw Beans.

Although I don't have too much information available on this interesting vegetable, I wanted to put up a page with photographs so that people curious about it could at least see what it looks like. The name becomes obvious when you look at the picture to the left (click on the picture to see a larger version) – cut into a cross section, you can see the "wings."

In Thailand, I've encountered winged beans mostly in a salad of the yam variety with a hot and sour dressing. Kasma taught a version of this recipe as Winged Bean Salad with Toasted Coconut, Peanuts and Limy Chilli Dressing (Yam Tua Poo) in Advanced Series Set A (class 2). In addition, winged beans also are found served raw to be eaten with lahb, the fiery salad from northeastern Thailand (Northeastern-Style Spicy Minced Chicken Salad – Lahb Gkai). In the south of Thailand they show up on the vegetable platters that are served with nearly every meal.

Winged beans are difficult to obtain where we live, in the San Francisco Bay Area. In the warmer summer months (late July, August) there are two ethnic markets in East Bay (one in Oakland, one in Richmond) where we can occasionally find them. In her recipes, Kasma usually substitutes snow peas, 2 to 3 snow peas per winged bean.
